text:
maria: Heads-up — AcmeCorp Dedicated asked for a staged cutover plan: they want to shift traffic to a new model variant over 3 weeks (1% -> 10% -> 50%) but with strict per-customer isolation and per-route quotas. Can we offer dynamic throttles + an automated safe fallback?

alex: Short answer: yes. Long answer: we need three pieces — per-tenant rate windows, a tenant-level circuit breaker, and a console-level pause/rollback. Also need telemetry hooks so the dashboard can surface deltas.

jordan: SRE perspective: Agree with alex. Add automatic rollback rules: if tenant error_rate > 3% for 5m OR p99 latency regresses > 2x baseline, cut canary to 0 and notify oncall. Also we need an emergency kill-switch that works at edge (before runtime queuing) so customer traffic never floods backend.

leo: Product note: Customers will expect to set safety thresholds themselves in the Console (not just ops). UX should let them define an SLA guard: {metric, window, threshold, action} — action = throttle/fallback/notify. Prefer actions to be composable.

maria: Proposed config sketch I sent offline; pasting a trimmed example for discussion:
```
canary: {
  scope: "tenant",
  steps: [1, 10, 50],
  step_duration: "72h",
  max_qps: 200,
  fallback_model: "v1-stable",
  circuit_breaker: {error_rate_pct: 3, p99_ms: 1200},
  telemetry_tags: ["tenant_id","route","model_variant"]
}
```

alex: Implementation notes: we can reuse policy-service routing rules but need to extend API to accept scope=tenant and the circuit_breaker block. We'll need a small state machine to advance steps and to pause/rollback on triggers. Also bucket quotas by tenant to enforce isolation.

jordan: On monitoring: required graphs per-tenant: requests/s, errors/s, error_rate_pct, p50/p95/p99 latency, token_cost/s. Need a canary-diff view that overlays baseline vs canary for quick triage.

leo: UX asks: 1) live traffic slider (pause/resume) 2) pre-checklist before ramp (quota capacity, acceptable error baseline, model size/latency delta), 3) audit trail for each step.

maria: Ops question: how do we surface per-tenant quota hits without spamming alerts? Suggest we emit a single "quota_near_limit" signal with severity levels and only alert if it crosses a threshold OR coincides with increased errors. Thoughts?

alex: That sounds reasonable. We'll tag telemetry with tenant and route, then build alert rules that require AND of (quota_near_limit AND error_rate > X) to fire paging. Low-sev logs still go to infra channel.

jordan: Checklist for prototype: 
- policy-service: tenant scope + circuit breaker
- runtime: fast-path kill switch + fallback routing
- console: canary stepper UI + safety thresholds
- metrics: per-tenant p99, error rate, token cost
- runbook: rollback/playbook per-customer

deploy-bot: Deploy plan created: acme-dedicated/cutover-proto-1980064321; target env: staging -> canary harness enabled.

maria: Can we target a small prototype this week to demo UX + automated rollback? Asking for sign-off from @leo and @alex. :thumbsup: or :no_entry_sign:?

leo: :thumbsup: I can carve out time to review the UX prototype Friday.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll spin up the policy change branch and wire basic telemetry.

jordan: I'll draft the runbook and add the alert conditions.

maria: Great — thanks all. I'll follow up with a short PRD + acceptance criteria.
